entries.en: Ha! I bet you did, too.
Shut up, Fredricks.
Calm down, Private, this isn't an inspection.
Right, sorry. What can I do for you, Commander?
Thank you. You too.
I, ah, well, she's an asari who works here as... that is, she helps people with... things.
Ha! You never went to see her, did you, Private?
I, uh, no. I never did. I couldn't afford it. It costs half a year's credits just to go in and talk to her.
Sure, she's across the bridge from the embassies.
Thanks, kid. Have fun. Try not to get into too much trouble.
I will. Have fun, that is.
Commander, good to see you again.
This place is amazing... Commander.
I think I'll see if I can get stationed here permanently.
Just saying hi. Enjoy yourself, Private.
What can you tell me about the asari Consort?
That's fine, Private. Just tell me where to find her.
Can you at least tell me where I can find her?
Consort?
Where is she?
Commander. What can I do for you?
Oh, Commander.
Relax, Private, this isn't an inspection.
Ha! You've never been, have you, boy?
You never went to see her, did you?
Did you really go to see the Consort?
You never went to see her, did you, Fredricks?
About twenty years ago, I was part of a mission in the Skyllian Verge. I was working with Saren to find and remove a known terrorist threat.
Saren eliminated his target. But a lot of people died along the way. Innocent people. And the official records just covered it all up.
But I saw how he operates. No conscience. No hesitation. He'd kill a thousand innocent civilians to end a war without a second thought.
I know how the world works, Commander. Sometimes you're forced to make unpleasant decisions.
But only if there's no other way. Saren doesn't even look for another option. He's twisted, broken. He likes the violence, the killing. And he knows how to cover his tracks.
He's just frustrated. The Council's always preaching that we need to be part of the galactic community. But for them it's a one-way street.
They want us to expand and settle unstable regions like the Skyllian Verge and the Attican Traverse. But when we run into trouble, they don't want to help us out.
Everyone knows it's only a matter of time until we get a seat on the Council. The ambassador just thinks it should happen sooner rather than later. And I agree.
Of course they would! If we did everything they told us to, they'd love to have us on the Council. But it wouldn't be much of a deal for us.
I understand their side. They don't want us dominating the Council. It's founded on cooperation and alliances. But we have to look out for our own interests, too.
If the Council passes a ruling on an interstellar matter, we have to follow it. We don't have the fleets or political allies to defy them.
Once we get a seat on the Council, we'll be able to influence those rulings, protect our own interests. No more jumping through hoops whenever we want something.
He's a necessary evil of galactic politics. Buying and selling information is part of the game, and the Shadow Broker just happens to be the best player on the field.
Always sells to the highest bidder. Doesn't get involved in politics. Doesn't pick sides. A simple system, but it works.
He's not a threat to anyone. Not directly. He's just a resource we can use. Or she is. Or maybe they are. Nobody really knows.
The guy joined C-Sec about twenty years ago. He's been an embarrassment to our species ever since.
Roughing up suspects in custody, bribery accusations, alcohol and drug use. The embassy used to step in when he got in trouble, but I guess enough was enough.
He was one of the first human C-Sec officers. Guess it would have looked bad if he got fired.
A lot of backroom deals were worked out over the years to keep him on the force. Politics is a dirty business sometimes.
But it looks like his time's run out. We've got enough humans in C-Sec now to stop protecting him.
Harkin may be human, but he's also an ass. He's had more than his share of chances.
If the embassy wasn't protecting him, he would've been fired fifteen years ago. C-Sec is better off without him.
He specializes in moving large sums of money without leaving a paper trail. A financial genius. Doesn't do anything illegal, but he knows all the loopholes.
He's got an impressive client list: ambassadors, diplomats, Spectres. That's probably why the Shadow Broker uses him.
You and Saren have a history. What happened?
Sometimes a thousand people must die so a million can live.
Killing innocents doesn't end wars. It causes them.
Our ambassador doesn't seem to get along with the Council.
Maybe they'd let us join the Council if we were more willing to cooperate with the other species.
Who cares if we get a seat on the Council? What's the big deal?
I want to know more about the Spectres.
You don't think much of Harkin.
The guy's a scumbag. He should have been cut loose a long time ago.
I thought this embassy was supposed to help humans.
Tell me about Barla Von.
Why protect him?
They abandoned him?
What about you and Saren?
Council and the Ambassador
Shadow Broker
So would I.
He's a monster.
We're too independent.
Why do we bother?
I knew he'd try to stir up trouble. But Harkin isn't as smart as he thinks he is. I was never a Spectre. Not really.
The Council sent Saren to keep an eye on me and evaluate my performance. Just like they sent Nihlus to keep tabs on you.
It's not something I'm proud of. I had a chance to become the first human Spectre and I failed. Saren made sure of that.
I'll be here if you need anything.
I trusted you. You betrayed me.
I think I deserve the whole story.
Harkin spilled your dirty little secret. He told me you were a Spectre!
You used to be a Spectre!
It's close to twenty years ago now. Ambassador Goyle was our representative here on the Citadel. Like Udina, she wanted to get a human into the Spectres. She chose me.
We had intel on a rogue scientist being funded by batarian interests. He was trying to set up a facility to develop illegal AI technology out in the Verge.
We tracked the scientist to a refining facility on Camala. He was hidden away somewhere inside, protected by an army of batarian mercenaries.
The plan was simple: sneak into the plant, capture the scientist, sneak back out. Quick, quiet, and a minimum of bloodshed.
Saren and I split up to cover more ground. Then, about halfway through the mission, there was a massive explosion in the refinery core.
Officially, it was ruled an accident. But I think Saren detonated it on purpose to draw off the enemy guards.
The explosion tore the refinery to shreds. The whole place was on fire. Black chemical clouds poured out into the atmosphere. Nobody inside survived.
There was a camp for the workers and their families nearby. Between the fires and the toxic fumes, the final death count was over five hundred. Mostly civilians.
Saren didn't care. The target was eliminated. Mission accomplished. And I ended up taking the blame. That ended all talk of me joining the Spectres.
In his report, Saren accused me of blowing his cover. He said it was my fault the guards were ready for us. He claimed that's why it turned into a massacre.
Saren's report was all the proof the Council needed to kill my chances of becoming a Spectre.
I don't. I blame Saren. I think he wanted things to go bad. He was looking for an excuse to blow that refinery.
Maybe he just likes the violence. Maybe he was just trying to make me look bad to keep humans out of the Spectres. If so, he pulled it off.
Who do you think the Council was going to listen to? Me? Or their best agent?
I had a bad feeling about him right from the start. I should've been more careful. Maybe I could have stopped things before they got out of hand.
You're right, Commander. It's no good living in the past. We need to stay focused on exposing Saren's current crimes.
Why weren't you honest with me?
Sounds like overkill to me.
Saren caused the explosion. How'd he pin it on you?
Don't blame yourself, Captain.
Why'd you let him get away with it?
The only thing I care about is stopping Saren.
I want to know the truth about you and Saren. I want to know about the mission you were on together all those years ago.
You worked with the Spectres.
Why hide this?
This doesn't matter.
You got blamed?
It wasn't your fault.
That's not fair!
Forget about the past.
But you're the one who can stop Saren. I believe in you, Shepard. If that means I have to step aside, so be it.
What can you tell me about Noveria?
Any extra intel you can give me on our colony at Feros?
What do you know about the Artemis Tau cluster?
Do you know anything about Virmire?
Artemis Tau Cluster
Where did you hear that name? Never mind. I don't want to know.
Banes is dead. Has been for quite some time.
I don't know much about it. You should talk to Admiral Kahoku. One of his crews discovered Banes' body.
Last I heard, he was up in the Tower trying to get the Council to investigate Banes' death.
You should mention Banes the next time you see him. See if he'll tell you anything.
Is there anything else, Commander?
Where can I find Admiral Kahoku?
What do you know about Armistan Banes?
The people I spoke with seemed to think he was still alive.
Any idea how to find him?
I might look into it later.
I spoke to Kahoku. He never brought it up.
Kahoku.
Banes?
That's strange.
If I have time.
I met him.
The colony tried to build on what the Protheans left behind. We lost all contact with them when the geth attacked.
Not much. I've never been there myself. A handful of systems with a few small uncharted worlds, but no real colonies.
Might not be easy finding Dr. T'Soni out there. My advice is to look for the world with the Prothean ruins.
Sorry, Shepard. I'd never even heard of it before all this. You'll have to go there and check it out yourself.
Noveria's trouble. Always has been. The whole planet's basically a center for corporations to conduct illegal research.
Watch your back there, Shepard. Spectres are about the only form of Citadel authority Noveria respects, but they aren't popular.
The entire planet used to be one giant Prothean city. Mostly ruins now, but some of the infrastructure is still intact.
Good luck, Shepard. I'll be over in the ambassador's office if you need anything else.
They're not your typical government agency. They tend to work alone, behind the scenes. They take care of problems the Council can't.
It's not easy preserving peace across an entire galaxy. The Council prefers to use diplomacy and negotiation, but sometimes more extreme measures are needed.
You can't just apply to join. There's no training program. Spectres aren't made -- they're born.
The Council's always looking for exceptional individuals. People who can get the job done, like you. They've been watching you for years.
They see something in you. They want you on their side. Nihlus was supposed to give them a final recommendation, but with him gone, things are still up in the air.
There is no command structure. Each Spectre answers directly to the Council. Sometimes they're sent on specific missions. Other times they act on their own.
They tend to operate outside the law. Do whatever it takes to accomplish their goals. And the Council just turns a blind eye. Spectres have a lot of power, Shepard.
It doesn't happen often. The Council is careful when they select their candidates.
But when something does go wrong, there's usually only one solution: send another Spectre to bring the rogue agent down.
Everything about them is classified. We don't even know how many there are. The latest Alliance estimate puts their numbers under a hundred.
